x: Belgrave's army sprinters Dave Armstrong and Lenny Paul distinguished themselves by powering their 4 man bobsleigh into the GB 1 slot at the Calgary Winter Olympics.
Newcomer Lenny Paul did the double in the 100m and 200m. Paul Cuff and Jay Busk had a head to head in the 400m with Paul just getting the verdict.

Joe Minetti won the Surrey Junior title and reduced his best to 10.8 while Mike Bazire, Dave Armstrong and Len Paul - a new member who trains with Dave and is a member of the British Bobsleigh Squad - were also under 11 seconds.

Marriage next too for fellow sprint star Lenny Paul who we understand is planning 'To tie the knot' before the '89 track season. Not to be left behind middle distance junior star, Darren Mead has recently announced his engagement to Donna.

Belgravians will immediately recognise the names of Dave Armstrong and Lenny Paul in the sprints and the distance running star John Wright. Eddy has recently been appointed official trainer of the British Bob-Sleigh teams and has sent in the following report.
Welcome to new members to our teams, Ossie Cham, Femi Abejide, Nigel Bevan and Lennie Paul. You are always assured of a great welcome to our Track and Field team.

Stars of the day were Lenny Paul who beat a good field in the 100m and John Regis who ran a blistering 45.4 sec. leg in the long relay. There were ten new faces in our team on the day and all felt that we were capable of much better.

100m: 1.J.Regis 10.65 (10.56 sf); 5.L.Paul 10.79 (10.70 sf); sf 5.P.Goedluck 10.84; 200m: ht 2.P.Goedluck 21.71; 400m; ht 7.J.Busk 49.68; 10000m: 3.G.Staines 28.12.93; HJ: 5.O.Cham 2.15; TJ: 2.F.Abejedi 15.86; SP: 10.A.Ekoku 15.70; JT: 4.N.Bevan 74.60.
Lenny Paul's top posting. As we enter the '91 T & F Season Lenny Paul takes up a new post as 'A' team Captain.

Lennie Paul was a clear winner in the 'A' 100 and 200, Abi in the 'A' discus, Andy Lloyd in the 'A' 1500, Paul Evans in the 'A' pole vault while Mike Edwards arrived jet lagged straight from the U.S.A. to set a pb and a new Club Record by winning the 'A' pole vault with 5.30.

Lenny Paul found himself outgunned by up and coming youngster Jason Livingstone in the 100 metres. Two days earlier in Limerick, Ireland, Lenny had comfortably beaten his rival 10.59 to 10.81 to win in the Ireland v England v Russia match, but back at the Palace Livingstone turned the tables to gain…

While Jon Ridgeon was running the B hurdles at the Parcelforce Games, and Mike Edwards was getting over 5.20, and Lenny Paul, Fred Salle and new signing Ikem Billy were in action, a member with a few more years services than those was also putting in an effort along the Crystal Palace home straight.

Marlon was presented with his award for man of the match by our own Marcus Adam with Lennie Paul doing the commentary over the PA. Many top athletes from our successful BAL team came along and their support was very much appreciated by our young team.
Darrin Morris was 6th in the discus, 54.06, and John Regis found himself shunted back to 4th in the short sprint in 10.52 with Lennie Paul 6th, 10.56.
The team managers offered up thanks to Lennie Paul (playing his usual Captain's role) and for Simon Shirley who demonstrated the value of a world class decathlete's presence in the team.
Lennie Paul won the 100 metres with the slight assistance of a 3 metre per second following wind to set a huge pb of 10.25, beating Olympian Darren Braithwaite by 6/100ths.
Marcus was knackered and rumour had it that Lennie Paul had run the previous night with a broken toe! Well, as it turned out, all of this was true.

Others for the masochist stakes were: Simon Shirley - gaining second in both the 'B' long jump and the 'B' javelin plus the sprint relay, Lennie Paul - sprints and relay, Paul Beaumont - 400 hurdles, 400 flat and long relay.

Marcello Bizio is at home on road, country or track; here he is on his way to 3rd in the BAL match 4 "B" steeplechase [b]. Track captain Lennie Paul blisters away from the 100m start on the first leg of a sprint double at Gateshead [a].
